items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I saw Cecil and a banjo player called Ikie come out of the back room... He asked me if I wanted to try and I did.

ctx.x: But my first experience with reefers came eventually. We were playing a matinee on a Sunday and I started drinking gin early in the afternoon and felt fine. This continued until the Savoy closed and I was feeling real groovy but not drunk. There was a bar on the corner of 132nd and 7th Avenue called Pete's, and naturally it catered to the theatrical people and musicians as it was near the Lafayette theater, the different clubs in the neighbourhood and the Rhythm club.

So I went to Pete's, ordered half a pint of gin and had drunk about half of it when I saw Cecil and a banjo player called Ikie come out of the back room and go in the toilet. For some reason I had an idea that something was up so I went in the toilet also. I saw Ikie taking out a cigarette and he said it was a reefer. He asked me if I wanted to try and I did. I took one big puff and held it in my lungs for a few seconds and another which I also held as long as I could, passed it to Cecil and went back to the bar.
Two minutes later I thought the world was caving in on
